drills.title: A delivery-fee chain
drills.prompt: Arrange the lines so the program prints the delivery fee: free from Rs. 499, Rs. 30 from Rs. 200, otherwise Rs. 50. The first two lines can go in either order. Two lines do not belong.
drills.explain: The condition sits in round brackets and each block in curly braces. The word is else if (not elif). The chain is checked from the top and the first true condition wins, so the biggest limit comes first and else catches everything left.

drills.title: Conditions, ternary and switch
drills.prompt: Fill the blanks so the program prints the goal output.
drills.explain: || is OR: a child under 5 or a senior of 60 and over gets the discount, and no age is both, so && would never be true. condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse picks one of two values. equalsIgnoreCase ignores capital letters, equals would not match Yes with yes. A switch expression needs a default for everything else.

drills.title: First match wins
drills.prompt: Read the code and type exactly what it prints, one line per line of output.
drills.explain: In an else if chain only the first true branch runs. 82 is at least 50, so Pass is printed and the Merit branch of the chain is skipped, even though 82 would also pass it. The next if is a new, separate question, so it runs on its own and prints Merit. The ternary picks the text after the colon because 82 is not at least 90.

drills.title: Half a question
drills.prompt: The shop delivers on the same day to Mumbai and Pune, but the program does not compile. Click the line the compiler complains about, then choose the fix.
drills.explain: || joins two true/false questions. "Pune" alone is a text, not a question, so Java refuses it (in Python it would be accepted and always count as true). Write the full question on each side of ||. Joining the two with && would ask for a city that is both at once.

drills.title: Review the AI's fee rules
drills.prompt: The shop's rules: Rs. 30 within 3 km, Rs. 50 within 7 km, Rs. 80 beyond, and free delivery for members OR orders of Rs. 499 and above. An AI assistant wrote this code. It compiles and runs, but tick the real problems (there are two).
code: // free delivery for members OR orders of Rs. 499 and above

issues.text: The 3 km branch can never run: a 2 km order is charged Rs. 50 instead of Rs. 30
issues.why: The chain is checked from the top and the first true condition wins. distanceKm <= 7 is true for every short distance, so the narrower <= 3 test must come first.

issues.text: The free-delivery rule uses && where the comment says OR, so a member with a small order still pays
issues.why: && needs both parts to be true, || needs one. The rule is isMember || orderValue >= 499.

non_issues.text: int fee has no starting value, so it may be uninitialised when it is printed
non_issues.why: Every branch of the if / else if / else chain assigns fee, so the compiler knows it has a value.

non_issues.text: The free-delivery check must be an else if of the first chain
non_issues.why: It is a separate rule that overrides the distance fee. Chained as an else it would be skipped whenever the distance rules matched, which is always.

non_issues.text: isMember must be compared as isMember == true
non_issues.why: isMember already is a boolean, so it can be a condition on its own. == true only adds noise.

drills.explain: Both bugs are silent: the program compiles and prints a plausible fee. With a chain, read the conditions from the top and ask which cases each one swallows. With a rule written in words, check every && and || against the words AND and OR.
